p: conceived: Man's nature, the estate of marriage, and God's blessing were not utterly abolished through sin, but the quality or condition of it was changed.
from the LORD: That is, according to the Lord's promise, as some read Ge 3:15, "To the Lord" rejoicing for the son she had born, whom she would offer to the Lord as the first fruits of her birth.

offering unto the LORD: This declares that the father instructed his children in the knowledge of God, and also how God gave them sacrifices to signify their salvation, though they were destitute of the ordinance of the tree of life.
accepted: Both you and your sacrifice shall be acceptable to me.
door: Sin will still torment your conscience.
desire: The dignity of the first born is given to Cain over Abel.
Am I my brother's keeper: This is the nature of the reprobate when they are rebuke for their hypocrisy, even to neglect God and outrage him.
voice of thy brother's blood crieth: God avenges the wrongs against his saints, though no one complains: for the iniquity itself cries for vengeance.
from the earth: The earth will be a witness against you, which mercifully received the blood you most cruelly shed.
fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou: You will never have rest for your heart will be in continual fear and worry.
My punishment is greater than I: He burdens God as a cruel judge because he punished him so severely.
vengeance shall be taken on him: Not for the love he had for Cain, but to suppress murder.
mark upon Cain: Which was some visible sign of God's judgment, that others should fear by it.
city: Thinking by this to be safe, and to have less reason to fear God's judgments against him.
two wives: The lawful institution of marriage, which is, that two should be one flesh, was first corrupted in the house of Cain by Lamech.
for I have slain a man: His wives seeing that all men hated him for his cruelty, were afraid, therefore he brags that there is none strong enough to resist, even though he was already wounded.
seventy and sevenfold: He mocked at God's tolerance in Cain jesting as though God would allow no one to punish him and yet give him permission to murder others.
call upon the name of the: In these days God began to move the hearts of the godly to restore religion, which had been suppressed by the wicked for a long time.
